title: ADA Health Policy Institute: Economic Outlook and Emerging Issues in Dentistry, 4th Quarter 2025

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: American Dental Association, Health Policy Institute (ADA is a professional and advocacy organization for dentists)
reliability: Primary survey by the dentists' trade and advocacy association; panel survey with 34.7 percent adjusted response rate and open-ended answers coded by the publisher. The ADA lobbies on dental insurance issues, so framing may favor providers. Publication month inferred from the survey being sent December 8, 2025.
findings: The survey was sent December 8, 2025 to 2,432 panel members; 839 responded (adjusted response rate 34.7 percent).

Asked for the top 3 challenges for their practice in 2026 (open-ended, 751 responses, coded): "Low insurance reimbursement / denials / Medicaid and Medicare / other insurance issues" 55.3 percent; staffing 54.2 percent; increasing expenses/overhead 41.5 percent.
"Spending too much time on administrative tasks" was a separate coded category at 0.8 percent of responses.
The report notes percentages for write-in categories should be used with caution.
limitations: The insurance category bundles reimbursement level, denials, Medicaid/Medicare and other insurance issues; it does not isolate eligibility verification or administrative time.
Self-selected panel of private-practice dentists (not staff who do the verification); no practice-size breakdown was read for this question.
The methods paragraph says "third quarter of 2025" in the methods paragraph although the report is titled 4th Quarter 2025; the date was taken from the survey send date.
Exact publication date not shown in the document text read (report year 2024 / December 2025 inferred).
